description: He does not throw you into a battle empty handed. He equips you — and the strength shows up when the battle does.
excerpt: There have been seasons where I have had to be strong. Not because I found it in myself. Because God armed me with it.
verse: "You have armed me with strength for the battle; you have subdued my enemies under my feet."
body_html:
I really like this verse.

Specifically the phrase you have armed me with strength for the battle.

Because it names something I have felt.

I am not just naturally strong going into a battle. I do not walk around ready for a fight. Honestly, I hate fighting. I would avoid most confrontation if I could. My default is peacemaker, or at least laugh maker, not warrior.

But there have been seasons where I have had to be strong. Not because I found it in myself. Because God armed me with it.

That is what this verse says.

He arms me.

He does not just tell me to go be strong on my own. He does not throw me into a battle empty handed. He equips me. He hands me the strength I do not naturally have. He fits it to me like armor before I walk out into the fight.

That completely changes how I think about hard seasons.

Because there have been times I have looked back and thought how did I even get through that? The years I could not have handled if you had described them to me ahead of time. The conversations I would have run from. The situations that required more than I had in me. And somehow, I stood. Somehow, I made it through. Somehow, I even walked through them with some grace.

That was not me.

That was God arming me.

He gave me strength I did not manufacture. He gave me words I did not prepare. He gave me a steadiness that was not naturally in my personality. He gave me a courage that was way beyond my normal capacity.

He armed me.

For the battle. In the moment I actually needed it. Not before. Not after. Right when I stepped into it.

That is such a comforting truth for anyone who feels like they are not the type of person who can handle what is in front of them.

Because David, the guy writing this psalm, was a warrior. He had killed a giant. He had led armies. He had been through more battles than most of us can imagine. And even he did not credit himself. He said You armed me.

If David had to be armed by God, then so do I. So do you.

We are not supposed to walk into our battles trusting in our own strength. We are supposed to walk in trusting the One who arms us. And when we do, we find that we are stronger in the fight than we were sitting on the sidelines.

The strength shows up when the battle does.

I have had to learn that. Sometimes I sit and worry about a hard conversation or a hard season coming up and I think I do not have what it takes for that. And I am usually right. I do not. Not on my own. But God does not give me the strength while I am sitting in my kitchen worrying about it. He gives it when I actually step into it.

That is His pattern.

He arms me for the battle. In the battle. Not before.

I hate fighting. I would rather peace. But I am glad that when the battles come, I am not standing there empty handed. My strength is not from me. It is placed on me by a God who has walked me through every fight I have ever been in.

And He will do it again.
question: What battle are you dreading right now, and can you trust that God will arm you for it when the moment actually comes?
